title: Eval & Quality Monitoring Demo - Orion Bio
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Orion Bio through the Evaluate / Quality Monitoring features (prompt set management, regression detection, A/B comparisons, and eval dashboards). Customer is focused on detecting regressions when changing models or prompt templates, and wants automated alerts, baseline prompt sets for clinical QA, and clear metrics for pilot success. Security questions (SOC 2, SSO, KMS) and deployment options (Dedicated vs Private/VPC) came up; Redwood to share pricing and Private deployment checklist and run an initial benchmark on a sample prompt set.
next_steps: Redwood to share pricing + Private deployment checklist (Alex) by 2025-04-04
Redwood SE to run eval benchmark on Orion sample prompts and return results (Samira) by 2025-04-09
Schedule technical deep-dive on security (Priya + Redwood Security) week of 2025-04-14
action_items: Samira Khan (Redwood SE): run eval benchmark using Orion sample prompt set (due 2025-04-09)
Alex Park (Redwood AE): send pricing sheet + Private deployment checklist (due 2025-04-04)
Dr. Maya Rios (Orion): share 50-100 representative prompts and expected outputs (due 2025-04-06)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Rios (Head of AI, Orion Bio), Ethan Cole (ML Engineer), Priya Singh (Security)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick housekeeping, this session is a demo of our Evaluate and quality monitoring capabilities, show the Console, the API, and some examples of regression alerts and A/B comparisons. Samira will do the deep-dive.
[00:16] Samira (Redwood): cool, yep, so we'll start with the prompt-set concept. Basically you create a prompt set which is an ordered list of prompts + expected outputs or eval functions, you can run it against historical outputs or on new model variants to detect regressions.
[00:34] Dr. Maya (Orion): great, quick question — is data stored by Redwood? we have, like, clinical text, so residency matters and we need to ensure no PII leaves prem, um, without controls.
[00:48] Alex (Redwood): yes, good call — we discussed earlier, you can run Evaluate on Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployments; by default hosted keeps logs for X days but for sensitive data we'd recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS. we'll share the checklist.
[01:05] Ethan (Orion): and the eval — can it run on batches? Our corpus is, like, 10k prompts, we don't want to stream one by one.
[01:12] Samira (Redwood): yeah, you can either call the API for batch eval or upload datasets via Console, the backend runs parallel jobs, it will compute metrics like exact match, F1, rouge, and custom scoring functions. also supports A/B comparisons where we run prompt set on model A and model B and show pairwise deltas.
[01:36] Priya (Orion): for compliance, do you produce audit logs for eval runs and who accessed prompt sets?
[01:42] Alex (Redwood): yes, audit logs are part of the Console; RBAC and SSO via SAML are supported, and logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[01:50] Samira (Redwood): jumping into the Console — ok screen share, so here's the Eval dashboard, top-level metric, you can pick a prompt set on the left, choose baseline model, choose candidate models, and select thresholds for regression alerts. if metric drops below X% you can get email/Slack/webhook alerts.
[02:15] Samira (Redwood): note, sometimes product auto transcribes long function names as wrong, like K-V cash, but it's actually KV cache, mm — we optimize caching for generation performance but for Evaluate we typically run stateless scoring jobs.
[02:29] Dr. Maya (Orion): what about false positives on regressions — e.g., model randomness causes a couple of failures but not systemic?
[02:36] Samira (Redwood): good point; we provide confidence bands and you can set rolling windows, and require X consecutive runs or a z-score threshold. plus you can define ignore-rules for non-deterministic prompts or fuzz match scoring.
[02:52] Ethan (Orion): ok, show us an example A/B.
[02:55] Samira (Redwood): sure — run prompt set 'Clinical-QA-v1' against Model A (open model v1) and Model B (quantized variant). here's the pairwise results: Model B has slightly lower exact match on section extraction but better latency/cost. we surface a per-prompt delta table so you can pivot to problem prompts and tag them for follow-up.
[03:22] Alex (Redwood): customers like that because it ties model economics to quality, you can see cost per 1k tokens vs quality delta.
[03:30] Dr. Maya (Orion): and the alerting — can it trigger a rollback or automatic switch to a fallback model?
[03:36] Samira (Redwood): yes, through our rollout/route policies you can implement automatic fallback to a baseline model or route traffic to a higher tier when a regression is detected; we usually recommend canary first.
[03:48] Ethan (Orion): will that work on Dedicated? on Private?
[03:52] Alex (Redwood): yes, the same control plane can manage Dedicated or Private instances, the route policies are consistent across deployments.
[03:58] Priya (Orion): about retention — how long do eval artifacts live, and can we export them for our own archive?
[04:04] Samira (Redwood): by default eval results are retained 90 days on hosted, but for Dedicated/Private you can set retention policies or ship them to your S3/Blob storage; export is CSV/JSON or direct SIEM hooks for alerts.
[04:20] Dr. Maya (Orion): we want to measure precision/recall for extraction tasks and also hallucination rate for free-form summarization, can I plug custom metrics?
[04:28] Samira (Redwood): absolutely — the Eval API supports custom scorer functions, you can upload a small Python snippet or use a prebuilt metric and also do composite scores. we sandbox the code for hosted; on Private you can run arbitrary scoring.
[04:42] Alex (Redwood): also note you can create multiple prompt sets (dev, canary, prod) and tag them to routes so production traffic uses prod prompt set and canary traffic uses canary prompt set.
[04:56] [05:00] Samira (Redwood): walking through the sample prompt in Console — here's a prompt, expected output, gating rule (e.g., exact match > 0.9) — we can show per-prompt history and annotations. if a prompt regresses you can open a ticket from the UI and assign to a reviewer.
[05:18] Dr. Maya (Orion): how do we seed baselines? we have historic outputs from our previous model, can we import those?
[05:24] Samira (Redwood): yes import historical outputs as a golden set; the engine will compute baselines and trend lines. you can also pin a model version as the baseline.
[05:33] Ethan (Orion): latency measurement — does the eval include end-to-end latency from our app vs just token generation?
[05:39] Samira (Redwood): we capture request end-to-end if you use our SDK or attach tracing headers; otherwise we measure service-side latency. for user-facing SLOs we recommend distributed tracing hooks which we support.
[05:52] [06:00] Priya (Orion): security deep-dive — our legal wants SOC 2 and data residency; do you have SOC 2? and for Private, do you support HSM/KMS?
[06:08] Alex (Redwood): Redwood has SOC 2 in hosted; for Private we integrate with customer KMS and can support HSMs, we'll share the security pack. 
[06:18] Dr. Maya (Orion): if we run evals on hosted for non-PII, do you guarantee that prompt text isn't used to train models?
[06:26] Alex (Redwood): yes, we have clear data usage terms; for enterprise we can add contract language. technical detail: hosted eval data is used for diagnostics but not for model training by default — we'll confirm exact wording in the security docs.
[06:40] [07:00] Samira (Redwood): demoing the API: you can POST a prompt set run, get back a job id, poll or subscribe to webhook for completion, results include per-prompt metrics and attachments (diffs, examples). show code snippet — Python and curl.
[07:18] Samira (Redwood): here's an example custom scorer — it's a fuzzy span-match, it'll compute overlap and return a score 0-1; set threshold and create alert rules in the UI.
[07:30] Ethan (Orion): how are A/B deltas computed? pairwise or aggregated?
[07:35] Samira (Redwood): both — we compute pairwise per-prompt deltas and then aggregated deltas with confidence intervals; you can slice by tag, prompt length, or cohort.
[07:48] Dr. Maya (Orion): what about versioning prompt sets? we expect iterative updates.
[07:53] Alex (Redwood): prompt sets are versioned; you can diff versions and replay older versions against newer models to see drift.
[07:59] [08:00] Samira (Redwood): showing alert config — you can set severity, notify channels, and require n-of-m runs before firing. also you can white-list or ignore specific prompts.
[08:14] Priya (Orion): is the webhook secure? can we sign payloads?
[08:17] Samira (Redwood): yes, we support HMAC signatures and can use mTLS for enterprise.
[08:24] Ethan (Orion): what's the cost model for eval — per-run? per-prompt?
[08:29] Alex (Redwood): eval pricing is typically per-eval-job or per-prompt-run depending on volume; for pilots we can offer credits. we'll include pricing sheet in follow-up.
[08:38] [09:00] Samira (Redwood): switching to A/B comparison UI — here's the delta chart, here's a waterfall showing which prompts contributed most to quality degradation. you can click into a prompt and see model outputs side-by-side.
[09:18] Dr. Maya (Orion): can human-in-the-loop labelers annotate and feed corrections to the eval?
[09:24] Samira (Redwood): yep, the review queue lets annotators provide gold labels, and those feed back into the prompt set for future runs. we also support gating so only approved annotations become the golden truth.
[09:36] Ethan (Orion): for our use case, we want to flag hallucinations — can we define a hallucination scorer?
[09:41] Samira (Redwood): you can implement a custom hallucination scorer or use combination heuristics (overlap to source docs, factuality model), and tag prompts for manual review.
[09:52] [10:00] Alex (Redwood): quick pause — any blockers from the compliance side?
[10:04] Priya (Orion): need to see SOC 2, data flow diagram, KMS options, and controls for who can access prompt sets. also retention and deletion APIs.
[10:14] Alex (Redwood): noted, we'll send security pack and schedule a follow-up with our security team.
[10:19] Samira (Redwood): continuing, here's an example regression alert email, includes direct link to the failing prompt and suggested next steps (re-run with higher temperature? or rollback).
[10:30] Dr. Maya (Orion): that link — we need SSO enforced, cannot be public.
[10:33] Alex (Redwood): yes SSO and RBAC enforced for all links in enterprise.
[10:38] [11:00] Samira (Redwood): demo of bulk eval — uploading CSV with 5k rows, start job, shows progress bar, sample errors for malformed rows, partial retries.
[11:16] Ethan (Orion): can we seed expected outputs programmatically?
[11:19] Samira (Redwood): yes via API or CSV import; you can map columns.
[11:24] [12:00] Alex (Redwood): question — what does success look like for your pilot?
[12:28] Dr. Maya (Orion): we want automated detection of regressions across our top 500 prompts, less than 1% false positive alerts, ability to identify problematic prompts and reduce hallucination rate by 20%. also need audit logs and SSO.
[12:46] Alex (Redwood): great, we can define those as pilot success metrics and instrument them in the run.
[12:52] Samira (Redwood): let's talk scoping — time to run 500 prompts depends on model latency; we can run them overnight or parallel. on Dedicated it's faster.
[13:06] Ethan (Orion): any options to cache results for stable prompts?
[13:10] Samira (Redwood): yes, prefix/KV caching helps for generation runs, but eval jobs are stateless; you can cache golden outputs to avoid re-eval costs.
[13:22] [14:00] Priya (Orion): legal will ask about contractual terms for Private deployment, support SLAs — can you share the enterprise pack?
[14:29] Alex (Redwood): yes we'll include enterprise pack and SLA options.
[14:36] Samira (Redwood): quick note — sometimes transcripts or auto tools mislabel product names; you'll see 'Redwood Optimize' in the Console, it's the cost/perf toolkit, not 'Redwood Optimizer' or 'Optimise', just a minor callout.
[14:50] [15:00] Samira (Redwood): quick live run — I will kick off a small prompt set 'demo-50' against two model variants so you can see the job lifecycle. starting job... job id 7b9f...
[15:12] [16:00] Samira (Redwood): job progressed, here's per-prompt table — prompt 12 failed exact match, opened the prompt detail, you can see outputs side-by-side and annotations.
[16:28] Ethan (Orion): can I export that failing prompt and share with my team?
[16:32] Samira (Redwood): yes export as JSON/CSV, includes model outputs, scores, and stack traces for failures.
[16:42] Dr. Maya (Orion): show me the alert config for thresholds again.
[16:47] Samira (Redwood): sure — threshold is 0.9 exact-match, require 2 consecutive runs or a p-value < 0.05. you can choose rolling-window 7 days.
[17:00] [18:00] Alex (Redwood): wrapping up — action items recap: Redwood will run a benchmark on the sample prompts, send pricing + Private checklist, and security will follow up.
[18:12] Dr. Maya (Orion): timeline — we'd like pilot to start mid-April if possible.
[18:18] Alex (Redwood): we'll aim to deliver benchmark by next Wednesday and schedule security call for week of Apr 14.
[18:25] Ethan (Orion): ok thanks, looking forward to results.
[18:30] Alex (Redwood): thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.
[18:36] [Call ended]
